text:
Abstract  
The European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) holds hundreds of thousands of raw sequencing runs for Escherichia coli (NCBI taxon 562). Understanding the experimental focus—whole‐genome sequencing (WGS) versus transcriptomic (RNA‐Seq) studies—guides resource allocation and data reuse. We queried ENA via its portal API for runs matching taxon 562 and library strategies “WGS” and “RNA-Seq,” respectively, each with a minimal limit parameter. We obtained total matching counts of 497,414 WGS runs and 13,838 RNA-Seq runs. Of the 551,679 total E. coli runs listed by BRC Analytics as of the query, 90.2% were WGS and 2.5% were RNA-Seq, indicating that WGS dominates publicly deposited E. coli sequencing data. These counts inform researchers of the available data types and highlight the relative scarcity of transcriptomic datasets in this species, suggesting areas for future data generation or targeted reuse.

I. Introduction  
Background. Escherichia coli is a model organism with extensive genomic resources. Raw sequencing runs deposited in ENA span various library strategies, notably WGS for genome assembly and RNA-Seq for transcriptome profiling. Quantifying these categories aids database users in understanding the available data landscape.  
Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.  
Knowledge Gap. The proportion of WGS versus RNA-Seq runs for E. coli in ENA was previously unquantified by computational query.  
Objective & Hypothesis. We sought to determine how many E. coli runs in ENA are whole‐genome sequencing as opposed to RNA-Seq, expecting WGS to predominate given its primary use in bacterial genomics.

II. Materials and Methods  
Study Design. We performed targeted API queries against ENA to count runs for taxon 562 with specific library_strategy filters.  
Materials. ENA portal search (via brc_ena_search function).  
Procedures.  
1. Query ENA for WGS runs:  
   • Function: brc_ena_search  
   • Arguments: taxonomy_id="562", library_strategy="WGS", limit=1  
2. Query ENA for RNA-Seq runs:  
   • Function: brc_ena_search  
   • Arguments: taxonomy_id="562", library_strategy="RNA-Seq", limit=1  
Statistical Analysis. Each total_matching value from the search responses was used as the count. Proportions were computed against the total_in_ena (551,679) reported by a separate brc_ena_runs call.

III. Results  
Table 1 presents the counts and proportions of E. coli runs by library strategy.  

Table 1: ENA run counts and proportions for E. coli (taxon 562)  
| Library Strategy | Count   | Proportion (%) |  
|------------------|---------|----------------|  
| WGS              | 497,414 | 90.2           |  
| RNA-Seq          | 13,838  | 2.5            |  

Findings. Among 551,679 total E. coli runs (BRC Analytics ENA proxy), 497,414 (90.2%) are WGS and 13,838 (2.5%) are RNA-Seq.

IV. Discussion  
Interpretation. WGS runs overwhelmingly dominate E. coli sequencing submissions, with transcriptomic data comprising a small fraction.  
Context. The counts align with ENA’s deposited library strategy metadata [1],[2].  
Limitations. The “library_strategy” field depends on submitter annotation, which may contain misclassifications or omissions; runs with other or missing strategy labels are not captured here. These data do not indicate experimental quality, read length, or downstream usage.  
Conclusion & Future Directions. WGS is the primary data type for E. coli in ENA; RNA-Seq is comparatively underrepresented. Future work could stratify WGS into platforms or assembly projects, or assess temporal trends in RNA-Seq submissions to identify growing transcriptomic interest.

References  
[1] ENA portal API search query for WGS runs. URL: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/search  
[2] ENA portal API search query for RNA-Seq runs. URL: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/search  

Acknowledgments  
We thank EMBL-EBI for the ENA data access via its public REST API.
